name: Oz
note: Concurrent constraint language whose design effort began in 1991, unifying logic, functional, object-oriented, and stateful programming; Oz 1 was first released publicly in 1995
typeSystem: Dynamic: a variable's type and value are initially unknown, and its type is determined when the single-assignment variable is bound to an Oz value. The value universe includes records, procedures, cells, objects, computation spaces, and finite-domain values.
runtime: Mozart compiles Oz to bytecode for the Mozart virtual machine. Mozart 1 provides the classic constraint and distributed-programming system; Mozart 2 introduced a redesigned 64-bit VM, but its initial release did not yet implement those two subsystems.

runtimes.name: Mozart virtual machine (ozengine)
runtimes.role: Executes compiled Oz bytecode and pickled application functors; Mozart supplies the standard constraint, concurrency, and distribution facilities.

runtimes.name: Mozart 2 VM
runtimes.role: Redesigned 64-bit successor virtual machine with an extension interface; its initial release omitted the constraint and distributed-programming subsystems present in Mozart 1.

compilers.name: ozc
compilers.role: Mozart's batch compiler; compiles Oz source to virtual-machine bytecode or pickled/executable functors.

concurrencyModel: Ultralightweight, preemptively scheduled threads coordinate through dataflow synchronization on single-assignment logic variables. Mutable cells and locks support stateful concurrency, while Mozart 1 also provides network-transparent distributed programming.

concurrencyExample.caption: A consumer waits until a concurrent thread binds X
concurrencyExample.source:
declare X
thread
   X = 42
end
{Show X}
